9926.summary: The President has agreed a loan of 4 millions from the Banco de Londres, paying 2 1/4 on deposits once the Government can dispose of them freely; surplus funds, in an amount Limantour is to name, are to go in gold to the Bank of England (exchange today 23 13/16; at 24 or more cash could be converted here into gold and sent to Camacho to be kept at the English bank), Limantour to say how; Camacho asks authority to have the bonds of the new loan printed in the U.S.; the President asks whether unfinished, unsigned bonds in the U.S. might lead to something like an injunction against Morgan. Please decide.
9926.en:
English, with the same hole as the Spanish reading ([?deposited] stands for the code word ampida, which the
contemporary translator also left blank). Two telegraphed words (te se, line 16) are not rendered, as in the
contemporary translation.

The President has agreed [to] a loan [from the] Bank of London [of] 4 millions. After a year (pasado año, literally "a year having passed"), when the Government
freely disposes of [its] deposits, the Bank will pay 2 1/4 [per cent interest]. The President agrees that the amount
of surplus funds that you indicate be [?deposited] in gold [at the] Bank of England, exchange rate today 23 13/16.
We believe that at 24 or more it could gradually be converted here from cash into gold and sent to Camacho for its
safe keeping [at the] English Bank; but in any case you will indicate the most convenient way to handle that position.

snip.cap: The first lines of the code telegram of 26 August 1899

system: A word code in Spanish dictionary words mixed with clear Spanish: only some words are coded (cotorro = Banco, remero = Presidente, sabio = que, crimenes = Bonos, garlopas abocados = E.U.). Code words keep Spanish endings (jirpeo = indicó, jirpee = indique;…
